data.narrative:
Living Carbon, a Series A biotech company founded by Maddie Hall and Patrick Mellor, has raised $36M to date. The valuation assessment draws on a comp universe of 3 public peers (RXRX, TEM, ONT.L) and 8 private companies in the Biotech & Health sector, including Colossal Biosciences, Abridge, Chai Discovery, New Limit, and Recursion Pharmaceuticals.

Stage-progression analysis provides the primary quantitative anchor. Using the $36M total raised as a proxy for post-money valuation and applying a 2.0x step-up multiplier typical of Series A to later-stage progression yields an implied valuation of $72M. This method is applicable given Living Carbon's current stage positioning. The peer-median approach cannot be reliably applied: while 8 same-sector peers exist, filtering by stage and valuation tier yields insufficient overlap (fewer than 3 datapoints). Public-comp anchoring via P/S multiple is likewise not viable, as Living Carbon's revenue is not disclosed—standard for private biotech at this stage.

The analysis supports a valuation range of $61M (low) to $83M (high), with a median of $72M. This range reflects one-directional methodology application and carries material uncertainty around revenue trajectory, IP strength, and competitive positioning relative to the identified peer set. The narrow methodological base underscores the importance of updating this analysis as the company approaches Series B or as additional financial disclosures become available.
